name: e2b (E2B Dev)
description: Open-source infrastructure for AI code interpreting and agent sandboxes. Provides SDKs (Python, JavaScript) + CLI for starting/managing sandbox environments. Hundreds of millions of sandboxes launched in production. Architecturally adjacent to Devin DevBox: per-session isolated execution environments with secure file/process APIs from a thin orchestration layer over a low-level VMM.

name: e2b's Firecracker substrate (e2b-dev/infra)
description: github.com/e2b-dev/infra is the Firecracker-based execution engine that powers E2B. Self-hostable via Terraform. Cloud-provider matrix: GCP (available), AWS (Beta), Azure (not yet), generic Linux (not yet). The closest public proxy to Devin DevBox internals, by reasoned analogy from Cognition's microVM-pattern blog post.

name: Sandbox primitive (E2B's atomic unit)
description: E2B's core abstraction is a 'Sandbox': start a fresh isolated environment, execute code/commands inside, read/write files, then dispose. Lifetime measured in seconds-to-minutes. Per-session isolation is the security boundary. Pattern: SDK call → orchestrator allocates a Firecracker microVM → guest workload runs → snapshot or destroy on completion.

name: llms.txt index pattern
description: E2B publishes a complete documentation index at https://e2b.mintlify.app/llms.txt for LLM-driven documentation discovery. Mirrors Devin's own docs.devin.ai/llms.txt convention — both target AI-agent consumers as first-class doc readers. Adoption signal: Mintlify-rendered docs sites are converging on this pattern.

name: Devin DevBox likely architectural pattern (inferred)
description: By reasoned analogy from (1) Cognition's blog explicitly describing 'microVM isolation' and 'hypervisor-level snapshotting' for Devin sessions and (2) E2B's published Firecracker-based architecture serving the same problem domain, Devin DevBox plausibly runs each session in a Firecracker microVM with snapshot-based fast-start. STRONG-HINT, NOT DEFINITIVE — Cognition has not publicly named Firecracker. Useful as an interview-prep reasoning anchor: 'if the substrate is Firecracker-class, then the failure modes you'd debug are X, Y, Z.'

name: Snapshot fan-out (warm-template) pattern
description: Pattern shared across AI-agent sandbox systems (E2B, Devin-likely, Modal, etc.): take a snapshot of a fully-booted, dependencies-installed microVM, then fan out N clones from it for incoming user sessions. Each clone gets unique TAP/vsock/MMDS but shares the warm template's memory image (MAP_PRIVATE COW). Achieves <100ms session start vs cold-boot's ~125ms+kernel+app init.

name: SDK-over-sandbox-API abstraction layer
description: User-facing SDK (Python/JS for E2B) abstracts away the underlying VMM control plane. SDK call sandbox.run('ls /') translates to: orchestrator picks a warm clone → opens vsock channel → dispatches command → returns stdout. Devin's tool API is plausibly the same shape — the user/agent doesn't see Firecracker, they see Sandbox.method().

name: CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail) — case study in why microVM isolation matters
description: Recent (Apr 2026) CVE that affected container-isolated sandboxes. E2B published a blog post explaining their Firecracker-based sandboxes weren't affected — direct evidence that microVM isolation provides defense-in-depth that container runtimes don't. Useful interview-prep talking point: 'why does Devin run in a microVM and not just a Docker container?'
